cases.description: Verify that a normal ASCII password is encrypted using the APR‑1 algorithm and the result starts with the APR1 prefix and follows the expected salt+hash format.

group: Normal operation – password with special characters

cases.description: Ensure that passwords containing symbols are processed correctly and produce a valid APR‑1 hash.
An empty string should still be accepted and result in a valid APR‑1 hash (the algorithm treats an empty password as a zero‑length byte array).
Passing a null reference must cause a NullPointerException because the method attempts to call getBytes() on the argument.

group: Consistency – same password produces different salts

cases.expected: Two successive calls return strings with different 8‑character salts (the part after '$apr1$' and before the second '$').
cases.description: When no explicit salt is supplied, the implementation generates a random salt; verify that two calls with the same password yield different salts, confirming the random‑salt branch is exercised.
Confirm that the method uses the APR‑1 specific prefix, not the generic MD5 prefix.

cases.expected: String that matches the APR‑1 pattern '^\$apr1\$[./0-9A-Za-z]{8}\$[./0-9A-Za-z]{22}$'
cases.description: The method must correctly encode Unicode characters using UTF‑8 before hashing; the output should still be a valid APR‑1 hash.

A password consisting of 255 ASCII 'a' characters is the typical maximum length accepted by many authentication systems. The method should handle it without error and produce a correctly formatted APR‑1 hash.
A password of length 255 characters should be processed without error and produce a valid APR‑1 hash.
A very long password (5000 characters) should not cause overflow or performance issues and still produce a correctly formatted APR‑1 hash.

group: Special characters – password containing dollar signs

cases.description: Passwords that include the '$' character should be handled correctly without breaking the hash format.
Emoji characters are multi‑byte UTF‑8 sequences; the method must encode them correctly and still produce a valid APR‑1 hash.

group: Result structure – correct number of sections

cases.expected: Result contains exactly three '$' characters (i.e., splits into four parts: empty prefix, 'apr1', 8‑char salt, 22‑char hash).
cases.description: Ensures the APR‑1 hash string follows the expected '$apr1$<salt>$<hash>' structure.

group: Result structure – salt character set validation

cases.expected: All characters of the salt (the 8 characters after the first '$apr1$') belong to the set [./0-9A-Za-z].
cases.description: Verifies that the generated salt uses only the allowed Base64‑like character set.

cases.expected: The hash part (the substring after the second '$') is exactly 22 characters long.
cases.description: Confirms that the APR‑1 hash component has the correct fixed length.
